title: 得益于 GTA VI，Rockstar 移动游戏下载量增长超过四倍
content:
Rockstar’s mobile downloads more than quadrupled thanks to GTA VI – Mobilegamer.biz
Skip to content
GTA 6 launched on November 19, but Rockstar’s older games were already picking up on mobile in the run-up to its release and continued to gather pace over the launch weekend.
According to
AppMagic
estimates, Rockstar’s mobile games were downloaded roughly 90,000-140,000 times a day across iOS and Android from late October to mid-November. That rose to over 223,000 on November 18, the day before GTA 6 launched on consoles, and passed 600,000 a day over the weekend.
Vice City has seen the biggest jump. AppMagic counts the original paid game and the free Definitive edition (which costs £18.99 to unlock in full) together, and between them they went from 20,000-30,000 downloads a day in late October to around 270,000 by the weekend. That’s 1.8m downloads in the last 30 days.
Revenue is up too, from around $2,500-$3,000 a day to around $12,000. In total, Vice City made an estimated $130,466 over the 30 days.
GTA: Liberty City Stories has also surged, from around 25,000 to 35,000 downloads a day to around 165,000, with 1.4m downloads in the last 30 days. Chinatown Wars rose from around 10,000 to 15,000 a day to around 80,000, while Bully: Anniversary Edition climbed from around 12,000 to 17,000 a day to around 35,000, and GTA III – Definitive from around 4,000 to 7,000 to around 46,000.
San Andreas and Vice City returned to the top ten iPhone paid games chart in the US this weekend.
The older, cheaper mobile ports are doing well in the paid charts too. On November 23, the original Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is second in the US iPhone paid chart, with the original Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, a separate paid app from the free Definitive version, in ninth.
On Google Play in the US, San Andreas was second and Vice City sixth among paid games.
San Andreas and Vice City also returned to the US top ten paid charts on Google Play.
The original San Andreas made an estimated $391,876 in the last 30 days, and was making around $40,000 a day by November 22, up from $7,000 to $9,000 in late October. San Andreas – Definitive made $99,367, and its daily takings have roughly quadrupled to around $9,500.
AppMagic estimates that Rockstar’s mobile games have made $109.3m in lifetime revenue and been downloaded 212.6m times. As we reported last week, the
GTA games had earned Rockstar about $96m
shortly before the launch of GTA VI.
